object.title: Disjoint-union conjecture for oriented cycles
object.statement:
Let $C_1,\ldots,C_t$ be orientations of undirected cycles, and let $C_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}C_t$ be their disjoint union.

**Disjoint-union conjecture for oriented cycles.** Any disjoint union of orientations of cycles is $\delta^+$-maderian.

This would generalize the known result for disjoint unions of digons and the paper's result for a single oriented cycle; its resolution is not stated in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Lior Gishboliner, Raphael Steiner and Tibor Szabó, “Oriented cycles in digraphs of large outdegree”, arXiv:2008.13224 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.13224

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2020).

object.title: Combinatoriality of lattice sheaf cohomology vanishing
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a hyperplane arrangement in a vector space of dimension $\ell$, let $L_0$ be its intersection lattice with the minimal element removed, and let $\mathscr{D}$ denote the lattice sheaf associated with the module of logarithmic vector fields. **Lattice sheaf cohomology conjecture.** The vanishing of the groups

$$
H^n(L_0,\mathscr{D})
$$

for $0<n<\ell-1$ depends only on the poset $L_0$. This is the reformulation of Terao's freeness conjecture given by the authors, connecting freeness to the cohomology of a sheaf on the intersection lattice. The parser supplies no resolution evidence, so the claim is recorded as open.
object.source_name: Paul Mücksch, “On Yuzvinsky's lattice sheaf cohomology for hyperplane arrangements”, arXiv:2008.13700 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.13700

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2020). “This conjecture still remains open.”

object.title: Mohar's conjecture on the crossing number of antipodal multipartite graphs
object.statement:
Let $M_{n,t}$ be the graph considered in the construction above, and write $k=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. If a set $P'\subseteq P$ has strength $0$ and $t=|P\setminus P'|$, then the construction gives a drawing of $M_{n,t}$ with $H(n)-\tfrac{1}{2}t(k-1)(k-2)$ crossings. **Mohar's conjecture.** The crossing number of $M_{n,t}$ is equal to

$$
H(n)-\tfrac{1}{2}t(k-1)(k-2).
$$

This conjecture asserts that the displayed construction is optimal for these graphs; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status is open.
object.source_name: Bojan Mohar, “On a conjecture by Anthony Hill”, arXiv:2009.03418 (2020).

object.title: The inverse relationship between Zeroing Algorithm runtime and $Q_0(r)$
object.statement:
Let $Q_0(r)$ be the quantity associated with the initial polynomial in the Zeroing Algorithm, and let the run-time denote the number of steps taken by that algorithm.

**Inverse-relationship conjecture.** $Q_0(r)$ and the run-time have an inverse relationship.

This conjecture is motivated by simulations and by the preceding theorem, which suggests that the run-time becomes unbounded as $Q_0(r)\to 0^-$. The source does not specify a precise functional meaning of “inverse relationship” or provide a proved bound.
object.source_name: Thomas C. Martinez, Steven J. Miller, Clayton Mizgerd, Jack Murphy and Chenyang Sun, “Generalizing Zeckendorf's Theorem to Homogeneous Linear Recurrences, II”, arXiv:2009.07891 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.07891

object.title: Nonexistence conjecture for primitive graphs with prime distance sequence
object.statement: A **primitive graph** is a graph whose automorphism group acts primitively on its vertices, and its **distance sequence** records the distinct finite and infinite distances from a vertex. Let $p$ be a prime. **Prime-distance nonexistence conjecture.** There does not exist a primitive graph with distance sequence $1,\aleph_0,p$ for primes $p$. This conjecture is proposed as part of the classification of distance sequences for primitive graphs; its status is unresolved in the supplied source.
object.source_name: Katalin Berlow, “Distance Sequences of Locally Infinite Primitive Graphs”, arXiv:2009.11276 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.11276

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2020).

object.title: Fractional Akiyama–Watanabe conjecture for triangle-free planar graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a triangle-free planar graph, and let $\fva(G)$ denote its fractional vertex-arboricity. **Fractional Akiyama–Watanabe conjecture.** Every triangle-free planar graph has fractional vertex-arboricity at most $8/5$, that is, 
$$
\fva(G)\leq \frac{8}{5}.
$$
 This generalizes the Akiyama–Watanabe conjecture from bipartite planar graphs to the weaker triangle-free condition. The corresponding induced-forest conjecture remains open; the paper records the best known partial bounds and proposes this fractional strengthening.
object.source_name: Marthe Bonamy, František Kardoš, Tom Kelly and Luke Postle, “Fractional vertex-arboricity of planar graphs”, arXiv:2009.12189 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.12189

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2020). “We initiate a systematic study of the fractional vertex-arboricity of planar graphs and demonstrate connections to open problems concerning both fractional coloring and the size of the largest induced forest in planar graphs.”

object.title: Dichromatic-number conjecture for triangle-free digraphs with an oriented 2-star
object.statement:
Let $\overleftrightarrow K_2$ be the complete symmetric digraph on two vertices, let $\overrightarrow C_3$ be the directed 3-cycle, and let $S^+_2$ be the oriented 2-star. For a family $\mathcal F$ of forbidden induced subdigraphs, write $\operatorname{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathcal F)$ for the class of digraphs containing no member of $\mathcal F$ as an induced subdigraph, and let $\vec\chi$ denote dichromatic number. **Dichromatic-number conjecture.**

$$
\vec\chi\bigl(\operatorname{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\overleftrightarrow K_2,\overrightarrow C_3,S^+_2)\bigr)=2.
$$

The source explicitly says that this case is unsettled: it is not known whether the corresponding forbidden set is heroic.
object.source_name: Pierre Aboulker, Pierre Charbit and Reza Naserasr, “Extension of Gyarfas-Sumner conjecture to digraphs”, arXiv:2009.13319 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.13319

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2020).

object.title: Monotonicity conjecture for completeness in families of positive linear recurrence sequences
object.statement:
Let $g,k$ be nonnegative integers and $N$ an integer, and consider the positive linear recurrence sequences associated with the coefficient lists

$$
[\underbrace{1,\dots,1}_{g},\underbrace{0,\dots,0}_{k},N]
\quad\text{and}\quad
[\underbrace{1,\dots,1}_{g+1},\underbrace{0,\dots,0}_{k},N].
$$

**Monotonicity conjecture.** If the sequence generated by $[\underbrace{1,\dots,1}_{g},\underbrace{0,\dots,0}_{k},N]$ is complete, then so is the sequence generated by $[\underbrace{1,\dots,1}_{g+1},\underbrace{0,\dots,0}_{k},N]$. The authors motivate this from observed numerical behavior: for fixed $k$, the maximal admissible $N$ increases with $g$ and eventually becomes constant. A general proof remains open.
object.source_name: Elżbieta Bołdyriew, John Haviland, Phúc Lâm, John Lentfer, Steven J. Miller and Fernando Trejos Suárez, “Completeness of Positive Linear Recurrence Sequences”, arXiv:2010.01655 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.01655

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

object.title: The soficity conjecture for finitely generated groups
object.statement: A group is **sofic** when every finitely generated group can be homomorphically embedded into a metric ultraproduct of permutation groups. Let $\mathcal{S}=(S_n,\|\cdot\|_H)$, where $\|\sigma\|_H=\frac{1}{n}\|\operatorname{supp}(\sigma)\|$ is the normalized Hamming norm, and let $\mathcal{S}^*_{\mathrm{met}}$ be its metric ultraproduct. **The soficity conjecture.** Every group is sofic; equivalently, every finitely generated group can be homomorphically embedded into $\mathcal{S}^*_{\mathrm{met}}$. This is presented as the main open problem concerning metric ultraproducts and sofic groups.
object.source_name: Jakub Gismatullin, Krzysztof Majcher and Martin Ziegler, “Metric ultraproducts of groups – simplicity, perfectness and torsion”, arXiv:2010.03394 (2024).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.03394

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2020). “The main open problem is the following conjecture.”

object.title: The noncrossing matching ensemble realization conjecture
object.statement:
A **matching ensemble** is a collection of matchings satisfying the linkage axiom; it is **noncrossing** when its matchings are noncrossing. A **generic simple polypositroid** is a generic simple polypositroid $P$, and let ${\mathcal E}(P)$ denote the matching ensemble appearing in the paper's theorem.

**Noncrossing matching ensemble realization conjecture.** Every noncrossing matching ensemble appears as ${\mathcal E}(P)$ for some generic simple polypositroid $P$.

This conjecture asks whether the construction from generic simple polypositroids realizes all noncrossing matching ensembles. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
object.source_name: Thomas Lam and Alexander Postnikov, “Polypositroids”, arXiv:2010.07120 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.07120

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

object.title: The mixed metric dimension bound for graphs
object.statement:
Let $G\ne C_n$ be a graph, and let $c(G)$ denote its cyclomatic number. The quantity $L_1(G)$ is the parameter used in the mixed metric dimension bound, and $\mathrm{mdim}(G)$ denotes the mixed metric dimension of $G$. **Mixed metric dimension conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{mdim}(G)\leq L_1(G)+2c(G).
$$

The bound is established in the paper for cactus graphs, including trees and unicyclic graphs, where the number of edge-disjoint cycles equals the cyclomatic number. The conjecture asks whether the same inequality holds for general graphs; the supplied source gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Jelena Sedlar and Riste Škrekovski, “Mixed metric dimension of graphs with edge disjoint cycles”, arXiv:2010.10487 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.10487

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

object.title: Monotonicity conjecture for the number of galled networks
object.statement: Let $\mathrm{GN}_{n,k}$ denote the number of galled networks with parameters $n$ and $k$. **Monotonicity conjecture.** The sequence $\mathrm{GN}_{n,k}$ is increasing for $0\leq k\leq n$ and decreasing for $n\leq k\leq 2n-2$. This conjecture describes the expected monotonicity of the number of galled networks as the parameter $k$ varies; the paper states that the claims are not needed for its subsequent results and that proofs might appear elsewhere.
object.source_name: Michael Fuchs, Guan-Ru Yu and Louxin Zhang, “Asymptotic Enumeration and Distributional Properties of Galled Networks”, arXiv:2010.13324 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.13324

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

object.title: Nonexistence of a quadrisection of the six-dimensional torus by subcube partitions
object.statement: Let $T^6=(\mathbb{R}/4\mathbb{Z})^6=[0,4]^6/\sim$, and partition its $4^6$ subcubes into four classes. **Nonexistence conjecture.** No partition of the subcubes of $[0,4]^6/\sim$ gives a quadrisection of $T^6$. The paper explains that the symmetric construction used in odd dimensions fails because $4$ and $6$ are not relatively prime. It suggests that a less symmetric partition might exist but reports that trial and error indicates this is unlikely; no proof of nonexistence is given.
object.source_name: Thomas Kindred, “Efficient multisections of odd-dimensional tori”, arXiv:2010.14911 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.14911

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

object.title: Stanley's classification conjecture for indecomposable upho modular lattices
object.statement: Let $P$ be an **upho** modular lattice, meaning that $P$ is of finite type and its principal order filter at every element is isomorphic to $P$. Suppose that $P$ is indecomposable and contains a complemented interval of rank $3$. **Stanley's classification conjecture.** Then $P$ is isomorphic to the poset of submodules of $R^d$ of finite colength, ordered by reverse inclusion, for some local principal ideal domain $R$ with a finite residue field. This conjecture proposes that, apart from decomposable cases, these module posets account for upho modular lattices containing a complemented rank-$3$ interval; the paper records the conjecture but does not discuss its proof or status.
object.source_name: Yibo Gao, Joshua Guo, Karthik Seetharaman and Ilaria Seidel, “The Rank-Generating Functions of Upho Posets”, arXiv:2011.01916 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.01916

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

object.title: Balanced multipartite conjecture for decompositions of $k$-trees
object.statement: Let $k,n\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\{1\}$. Let $T$ be a **$k$-tree**, meaning a $k$-uniform tree defined recursively by starting with one edge and successively adding a vertex together with an edge containing it and a $(k-1)$-set from an existing edge. **Balanced multipartite $k$-tree conjecture.** If $T$ has $n$ edges, then the complete balanced $k$-partite graph on $kn$ vertices admits a decomposition into copies of $T$. This is proposed as a strengthening of the bipartite tree-packing conjecture attributed in the source to Graham and Häggkvist; the paper does not report a resolution, so the assertion remains open.
object.source_name: Stefan Ehard and Felix Joos, “Decompositions of quasirandom hypergraphs into hypergraphs of bounded degree”, arXiv:2011.05359 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.05359

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

object.title: Self-distinguishability conjecture for trees
object.statement:
Given a graph $G$, its **self-chromatic symmetric function** is $X_G^G$. Two graphs are **self-distinguishable** when their self-chromatic symmetric functions are different. For two non-isomorphic trees $T_1$ and $T_2$,

**Self-distinguishability conjecture.** $X_{T_1}^{T_1} \neq X_{T_2}^{T_2}$.

The conjecture asserts that trees are distinguished up to isomorphism by their self-chromatic symmetric functions. The paper reports verification for trees with up to $9$ vertices, while the general case remains open.
object.source_name: Nancy Mae Eagles, Angèle M. Foley, Alice Huang, Elene Karangozishvili and Annan Yu, “H-chromatic symmetric functions”, arXiv:2011.06063 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.06063

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

object.title: Categorification conjecture for higher Pascal triangles and their q-deformations
object.statement: Consider higher Pascal's triangles and the Catalan-number construction by algebraic complexes. **Categorification conjecture for higher Pascal triangles.** There exist constructions of algebraic complexes whose dimensions match the entries in the higher Pascal's triangles in the same way as for the Catalan numbers. Moreover, there exist $q$-deformations of these constructions that naturally give rise to $q$-deformed sequences such as those in Proposition 2. The statement proposes algebraic and $q$-deformed categorifications beyond the Catalan-number case; the source provides no proof or resolution.
object.source_name: Keke Zhang, “Generalized Catalan numbers”, arXiv:2011.09593 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.09593

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

object.title: Inclusion conjecture for broken-circuit, Gale, and quasisymmetric complexes
object.statement:
Let $\textbf{\textsc{bc}}$, $\textbf{\textsc{omat}}^{\operatorname{\mathsf{gale}}}$, $\textbf{\textsc{qe}}$, and $\textbf{\textsc{qi}}$ denote the corresponding classes of prefix-pure complexes. **Inclusion conjecture.** One has

$$
\textbf{\textsc{bc}}\subsetneq\textbf{\textsc{omat}}^{\operatorname{\mathsf{gale}}}\subsetneq\textbf{\textsc{qe}}\cap\textbf{\textsc{qi}}.
$$

The first inclusion is close to known results on broken-circuit complexes, and the conjecture holds for shifted complexes. The paper explains that the relevant inclusions into $\textbf{\textsc{qe}}$ and $\textbf{\textsc{qi}}$ are known, while the full strict-inclusion statement is not established.
object.source_name: Federico Castillo, Jeremy L. Martin and Jose A. Samper, “Hopf monoids of ordered simplicial complexes”, arXiv:2011.14955 (2024).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.14955

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2020). “It was proven in that every generic real-valued function on the ground set of a matroid, when extended linearly to bases, gives rise to a shelling order on the independence complex.”

object.title: The circulant orbit–eigenvalue conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be an uncoloured circulant graph. Write $V*V$ for the set of unordered pairs of vertices of $G$, and let $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ act on $V*V$ through its action on vertices. Let $r$ be the number of orbits of this action and let $s$ be the number of distinct eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix of $G$.

**Circulant orbit–eigenvalue conjecture.** The number of orbits of the action of $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ on $V*V$ coincides with the number of distinct eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix; equivalently, $r=s$.

This is stated as equivalent to the preceding conjecture in the uniform-coloured setting. The source gives no resolution, so the claim remains open here.
object.source_name: Isobel Davies and Orlando Marigliano, “Coloured Graphical Models and their Symmetries”, arXiv:2012.01905 (2025).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.01905

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

object.title: Bérczi et al.'s reduction conjecture for coverable matroids
object.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid whose ground set can be covered by $k$ independent sets; such a matroid is **$k$-coverable**. A **reduction** of a matroid is the reduction notion used in the source, and a **partition matroid** is a matroid whose ground set is partitioned into parts with independent sets meeting each part within its prescribed capacity. **Bérczi et al.'s conjecture.** Every $k$-coverable matroid can be reduced to a $2\cdot k$-coverable partition matroid. The conjecture asks whether reductions to partition matroids can always increase the covering number by at most a factor of two; the provided source does not state whether it has been resolved.
object.source_name: Kristóf Bérczi and Tamás Schwarcz, “Rainbow and monochromatic circuits and cuts in binary matroids”, arXiv:2012.05037 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.05037
